catalog_quote: Acento. El cuitlateco tiene un fonema suprasegmental, el acento (´) que unicamente vá en la última o penúltima sílaba; aún si la palabra es compuesta siempre tiene uno y sólo un acento. Ejemplos: dúhci maíz; duhcí ver; iwililúmɨ río. [PDF p. 11:] La mayor parte de las raíces son bisilábicas con acento en la última o en la penúltima sílabas; y hay algunas monosilábicas, y de más sílabas, éstas últimas hay que interpretarlas como antiguos compuestos. Las raíces terminan en vocal. ... Dos raíces se unen en una palabra única (con un sólo acento) gracias al proceso de composición radical.

new_statements.translation: Accent. Cuitlatec has one suprasegmental phoneme, the accent (´), which goes only on the last or penultimate syllable; even if the word is compound it always has one and only one accent. Examples: dúhci 'maize'; duhcí 'to see'; iwililúmɨ 'river'. [PDF p. 11:] Most roots are disyllabic with accent on the last or on the penultimate syllable; there are some monosyllabic ones, and ones with more syllables, the latter to be interpreted as old compounds. Roots end in a vowel.

new_statements.rule_in_words: Stress is a contrastive suprasegmental phoneme (minimal pair dúhci 'maize' vs duhcí 'to see'); it falls on either the final or the penultimate syllable of the word and is not otherwise predictable — a two-syllable right-edge window with lexically fixed placement. Every word, including compounds, has exactly one stress.
new_statements.secondary_stress: Not mentioned; the text says each word has 'uno y sólo un acento'.
new_statements.exceptions: None stated. Phrase-initial vowels take a glottal onset (not stress-related). Loanwords keep Spanish stress (fiskál, flóho, frastéru in the examples).
new_statements.domain_note: Word level: 'la palabra'; compounds ('aún si la palabra es compuesta') carry exactly one accent; PDF p. 11 restates it for roots ('la mayor parte de las raíces son bisilábicas con acento en la última o en la penúltima sílabas') and for compounds ('Dos raíces se unen en una palabra única (con un sólo acento)'). Inflected verb forms in the paradigms (PDF pp. 13-14) show the accent on the suffix (yuke-tí from yuké-), i.e. still within the final two syllables of the word. McQuown's snippet adds that the intensity accent is accompanied by a pitch rise ('alza tonal').
new_statements.identity_note: The source describes the Cuitlatec of San Miguel Totolapan, Guerrero (the last community; data from the last speaker Juana Can plus Hendrichs's 1930s materials), which is the only attested modern variety and corresponds to cuit1236 itself; the INAH repository metadata's geographic tag 'Atoyac de Álvarez' is a cataloguer's coverage tag for the historical territory named in the thesis introduction, not a different dialect. The file held by the project is the 1960 ENAH thesis; the Glottolog-listed 1962 INAH book is its published version and carries the identical stress sentence (Google Books snippet).
